items.title: Injective geodesic ray transform on a transversal manifold

references.title: Dos Santos Ferreira, Kurylev, Lassas, and Salo, The Calderon problem in transversally anisotropic geometries (2016)
references.locator: Section 1, CTA hypotheses and the injectivity condition on the transversal ray transform.

references.title: Mikko Salo, On geometric inverse problems and microlocal analysis (2023)
references.locator: Section 2.2, Theorem 2.7, injectivity of the geodesic ray transform on simple manifolds.

items.statement: Let $(M_0,g_0)$ be a compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. A nontangential maximal geodesic segment is a unit-speed geodesic $\gamma:[0,L]\to M_0$, with $L>0$, whose initial velocity points strictly inward at $\partial M_0$, whose terminal velocity points strictly outward at $\partial M_0$, and whose points for $0<t<L$ lie in $M_0^\circ$. For $f\in C_c^\infty(M_0^\circ,\mathbb R)$ define its geodesic ray transform by $I_{g_0}f(\gamma)=\int_0^L f(\gamma(t))\,dt$. The unweighted scalar ray transform is called injective on compactly supported smooth functions if $I_{g_0}f(\gamma)=0$ for every such segment implies $f=0$. For complex-valued $f$, injectivity means injectivity of its real and imaginary parts separately.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, with no orientability assumption. Fix a finite smooth atlas of interior and boundary charts and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it. For an integer $k\geq0$, define $H^k(M)$ as the completion of $C^\infty(M)$ in the sum of the Euclidean $W^{k,2}$ norms of the localized coordinate representatives; derivatives in a boundary chart are taken on the corresponding half-space. Define $H_0^1(M)$ as the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in $H^1(M)$. Define $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ by the fixed finite boundary atlas and partition of unity, using the Euclidean fractional Slobodeckij space $W^{1/2,2}(\mathbb R^{n-1})$ for each localized representative. Define $H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ as the continuous dual of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ with the Riemannian boundary density pairing. These are the fixed-atlas norms used on this page; no atlas-independence assertion is part of this definition.

items.statement: A transversally anisotropic product domain of dimension $n\geq3$ is a compact connected smooth $n$-dimensional Riemannian domain $(M,g)$ with smooth boundary, together with a compact connected smooth $(n-1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with boundary $(M_0,g_0)$ and an isometric embedding of $(M,g)$ as a smooth domain compactly contained in $(\mathbb R\times M_0^\circ,dx_1^2\oplus g_0)$. The coordinate $x_1$ on $\mathbb R$ is the distinguished Euclidean coordinate; $M_0$ is the transversal manifold. All Laplacians use $\Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\nabla_g$. Neither $M$ nor $M_0$ is assumed orientable. A positive smooth conformal factor is not included in this definition; claims using a conformally related metric must state and prove the required conformal transformation separately.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\geq3$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded smooth domain contained in a ball $B(0,R)$, and let $q\in L^\infty(\Omega,\mathbb C)$. There are constants $C>0$ and $\tau_0\geq1$, depending only on $n$, $R$, and $\|q\|_{L^\infty}$, such that for every $\zeta\in\mathbb C^n$ satisfying $\zeta\cdot\zeta=0$ and $|\zeta|\geq\tau_0$, there is $r_\zeta\in H^1(\Omega,\mathbb C)$ for which
$$u_\zeta(x)=e^{i\zeta\cdot x}(1+r_\zeta(x))$$
solves $(-\Delta+q)u_\zeta=0$ distributionally in $\Omega$, and
$$\|r_\zeta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\leq C|\zeta|^{-1}\|q\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|\nabla r_\zeta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
The dot product in the null-phase condition is complex bilinear, and $|\zeta|=(\sum_{j=1}^n|\zeta_j|^2)^{1/2}$.

items.statement:
Let $(M_0,g_0)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary and let $\gamma:[0,L]\to M_0$ be a unit-speed nontangential geodesic segment. For every real $\lambda$ and every $K>0$, there is a family $v_{\tau+i\lambda}\in C^\infty(M_0)$, $\tau\geq1$, such that
$$\|(-\Delta_{g_0}-(\tau+i\lambda)^2)v_{\tau+i\lambda}\|_{L^2(M_0)}=O(\tau^{-K}),\qquad \|v_{\tau+i\lambda}\|_{L^2(M_0)}=O(1),$$
and for every $\psi\in C(M_0)$,
$$\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\int_{M_0}|v_{\tau+i\lambda}|^2\psi\,dV_{g_0} =\int_0^L e^{-2\lambda t}\psi(\gamma(t))\,dt.$$
The statement permits transversal manifolds without an orientability assumption and makes no boundary condition assertion for the quasimodes.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a transversally anisotropic product domain, let $q\in C^\infty(\overline M,\mathbb R)$, and let $\varphi=\sigma x_1$ for $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$. For $0<h\leq h_0$ define
$$P_{\varphi,h,q}=e^{\varphi/h}h^2(-\Delta_g+q)e^{-\varphi/h}.$$
There is a constant $C$ such that every $w\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ satisfies
$$\|w\|_{L^2(M)}\leq Ch^{-1}\|P_{\varphi,h,q}w\|_{L^2(M)}.$$
Moreover, for every $F\in L^2(M)$ there is an $R\in L^2(M)$ solving $P_{\varphi,h,q}R=F$ in distributions on $M^\circ$ and satisfying
$$\|R\|_{L^2(M)}\leq Ch^{-1}\|F\|_{L^2(M)}.$$
No boundary trace is prescribed for $R$.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, and suppose the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$. For every $F\in L^2(M)$ and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ there is a unique weak solution $u\in H^1(M)$ of $(-\Delta_g+q)u=F$ with trace $f$. If $f=0$, $F\in H^m(M)$ and $m\geq0$ is an integer, then $u\in H^{m+2}(M)$ and $\|u\|_{H^{m+2}}\leq C_m\|F\|_{H^m}$. If $F$ and $f$ are smooth, this solution belongs to $H^m(M)$ for every integer $m\geq0$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, be a bounded smooth domain, let $\gamma,\widetilde\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive, let $x_0\in\partial\Omega$, and let $\xi_0\in T_{x_0}^*\partial\Omega$ have unit norm in the induced boundary metric. Choose a sufficiently small boundary patch and $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ supported there with $\chi=1$ near $x_0$. For every integer $N\geq1$ there are a smooth complex phase $\Phi$ in a collar of the patch and amplitudes $b_{\lambda,\gamma}$, $b_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma}$, defined for $\lambda\geq1$, such that
$$v_{\lambda,\gamma}=\lambda^{-1/2}e^{i\lambda\Phi}b_{\lambda,\gamma},\qquad v_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma}=\lambda^{-1/2}e^{i\lambda\Phi}b_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma},$$
have boundary values $\lambda^{-1/2}e^{i\lambda\phi}\chi$, where $\phi$ is real with $|d\phi|=1$ near $\operatorname{supp}\chi$, have $H^1(\Omega)$ norms bounded above and below by positive constants, and satisfy
$$\|\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla v_{\lambda,\gamma})\|_{L^2(\Omega)} +\|\operatorname{div}(\widetilde\gamma\nabla v_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma})\|_{L^2(\Omega)} =O(\lambda^{-N}).$$
Here $\phi=\Phi|_{\partial\Omega}$ is real, $d\phi(x_0)=\xi_0$, and $\operatorname{Im}\Phi$ is comparable to the inward distance to the boundary on the collar. Let $u_{\lambda,\gamma}$ and $u_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma}$ be the exact conductivity solutions with the same respective boundary values. Their corrections satisfy
$$\|u_{\lambda,\gamma}-v_{\lambda,\gamma}\|_{H^1(\Omega)} +\|u_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma}-v_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma}\|_{H^1(\Omega)} =O(\lambda^{-N}).$$
For every fixed integer $k\geq0$ and continuous $F$ on $\overline\Omega$, choosing $N>k$ gives
$$\lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda^k \int_\Omega \operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)^k F(x) \nabla v_{\lambda,\gamma}\cdot\overline{\nabla v_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma}}\,dx =c_k\int_{\partial\Omega}F|\chi|^2\,dS,\qquad c_k=2\int_0^\infty t^ke^{-2t}\,dt=\frac{k!}{2^k}>0.$$
The same limit holds with $v_{\lambda,\gamma},v_{\lambda,\widetilde\gamma}$ replaced by their exact corrections.

items.title: Scalar conductivity and Schrödinger Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps

references.title: Mikko Salo, Calderon problem, full lecture notes (2008)
references.locator: Section 3.1, conductivity and Schrodinger Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps and the physical flux convention.

references.title: Feizmohammadi and Oksanen, An inverse problem for a semilinear elliptic equation in Riemannian geometries (2019)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a nonempty compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary. For a real-valued $\gamma\in C^\infty(M)$ with $\gamma(x)>0$ at every $x\in M$, let $v_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gv_f)=0$ with trace $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, whose existence is supplied by the positive-conductivity solvability lemma. Define the full-data physical conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle=\int_M\gamma\,g(\nabla_gv_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})\,dV_g,$$
where $V_h\in H^1(M)$ is any extension of $h\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$. The weak equation makes this value independent of the extension. For smooth data, $\Lambda_\gamma f=\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v_f|_{\partial M}$; this is the full physical flux convention. When $M=\overline\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ with the Euclidean metric, this is the scalar Euclidean conductivity DN map.

For a real $q\in C^\infty(M)$ such that the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$, let $u_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $(-\Delta_g+q)u_f=0$ with trace $f$, whose existence follows from the nonresonant regularity lemma. Define the Schrödinger DN map $\Lambda_q:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_qf,h\rangle=\int_M\big(g(\nabla_gu_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})+qu_f\overline{V_h}\big)\,dV_g.$$
For smooth data this is $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}u_f|_{\partial M}$. Equality of these operators means equality on all of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, not equality for a restricted set of boundary inputs.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact transversally anisotropic product domain of dimension $n\geq3$ and let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. Fix an integer $s>n/2+2$ and a finite family $h_1,\ldots,h_m\in C^\infty(\partial M,\mathbb C)$. For $\epsilon=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_m)\in\mathbb R^m$ sufficiently near zero, the equation
$$-\Delta_g u+q u^3=0\quad\text{in }M^\circ,\qquad u|_{\partial M}=\sum_{j=1}^m\epsilon_jh_j$$
has a unique solution in a fixed small $H^s(M)$ ball. The parameter map $\epsilon\mapsto u_\epsilon$ is $C^3$ into $H^s(M)$, and the corresponding nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann data $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}u_\epsilon|_{\partial M}$ is $C^3$ into $C^0(\partial M)$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a transversally anisotropic product domain, let $q\in C^\infty(\overline M,\mathbb R)$, and let $\psi\in C^\infty$ be real on a neighborhood of the transversal projection of $M$, with $|d\psi|_{g_0}=1$. Suppose $a\in C^\infty(\overline M,\mathbb C)$ satisfies
$$2\partial_{x_1}a+2i\,g_0(\nabla_{g_0}\psi,\nabla_{g_0}a)+i(\Delta_{g_0}\psi)a=0.$$
Then, for all sufficiently large $\tau$, there is an exact solution
$$u_\tau=e^{-\tau(x_1+i\psi)}a+e^{-\tau x_1}r_\tau,\qquad (-\Delta_g+q)u_\tau=0\ \text{in }M^\circ,$$
with $r_\tau\in H^1(M)$ and $\|r_\tau\|_{L^2(M)}\leq C\tau^{-1}\|(-\Delta_g+q)a\|_{L^2(M)}$. No boundary value is prescribed for $r_\tau$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary. If $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ are strictly positive and $u_j$ solves $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma_j\nabla_gu_j)=0$ with smooth boundary value $f_j$, then
$$\langle(\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})f_1,f_2\rangle_{\partial M} =\int_M(\gamma_1-\gamma_2)g(\nabla_gu_1,\nabla_g\overline{u_2})\,dV_g.$$
If instead $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ have trivial Dirichlet kernels for $-\Delta_g+q_j$ and $u_j$ solves $(-\Delta_g+q_j)u_j=0$ with smooth boundary value $f_j$, then
$$\langle(\Lambda_{q_1}-\Lambda_{q_2})f_1,f_2\rangle_{\partial M} =\int_M(q_1-q_2)u_1\overline{u_2}\,dV_g.$$

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary, let $\gamma\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive, put $\rho=\sqrt{\gamma}$, and define $q=(\Delta_g\rho)/\rho$. If $v$ solves $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gv)=0$ and $u=\rho v$, then $u$ solves $(-\Delta_g+q)u=0$. The potential $q$ has trivial Dirichlet kernel. For boundary data $f=v|_{\partial M}$, with $\rho_b=\rho|_{\partial M}$ and the physical flux convention $\Lambda_\gamma f=\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v|_{\partial M}$, the exact boundary relation is
$$\Lambda_\gamma f=\rho_b\Lambda_q(\rho_b f)-\rho_b(\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}\rho)|_{\partial M}f.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary, let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, and let $\Lambda_q^{\rm NL}$ be the small-data nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for $-\Delta_g u+qu^3=0$. For smooth boundary directions $h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4$, let $v_j$ be the harmonic solution with boundary value $h_j$. If
$$w_{123}=\left.\partial_{\epsilon_1}\partial_{\epsilon_2}\partial_{\epsilon_3}u_\epsilon\right|_{\epsilon=0},$$
where $u_\epsilon$ has boundary value $\epsilon_1h_1+\epsilon_2h_2+\epsilon_3h_3$, then
$$-\Delta_gw_{123}+6qv_1v_2v_3=0,\qquad w_{123}|_{\partial M}=0,$$
and
$$\left\langle (D^3\Lambda_q^{\rm NL})_0[h_1,h_2,h_3],h_4\right\rangle =6\int_Mq\,v_1v_2v_3\overline{v_4}\,dV_g.$$

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $M\Subset\mathbb R\times M_0^\circ$ be a three-dimensional transversally anisotropic product domain with compact connected simple surface transversal $(M_0,g_0)$. For every $p\in M_0^\circ$ choose two nontangential unit-speed geodesic segments $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ meeting transversely at $p$ and nowhere else. For every $\xi\in\mathbb R$ and every $Q\in C^\infty(\overline M)$, there are four exact harmonic solutions $u_{\tau,1}^+,u_{\tau,1}^-,u_{\tau,2}^+,u_{\tau,2}^-\in H^1(M)$, with no prescribed boundary values, such that
$$\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\int_MQ(x_1,x')u_{\tau,1}^+u_{\tau,1}^-u_{\tau,2}^+u_{\tau,2}^-\,dV_g =c(p,\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\int_{I_p}e^{-i\xi x_1}Q(x_1,p)\,dx_1,$$
where $I_p=\{x_1\in\mathbb R:(x_1,p)\in M^\circ\}$ and $c(p,\gamma_1,\gamma_2)>0$ is the nonzero Gaussian normalization divided by $|\sin\angle(\dot\gamma_1(p),\dot\gamma_2(p))|$.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, be a bounded smooth domain, and let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive. items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a three-dimensional transversally anisotropic product domain with compact connected simple surface transversal $(M_0,g_0)$. Let $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(\overline M,\mathbb R)$. Suppose that for every finite family of smooth boundary directions, the corresponding small-data nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps for
$$-\Delta_g u+q_j u^3=0$$
agree for all sufficiently small real parameter values. Then $q_1=q_2$ on $\overline M$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a transversally anisotropic product domain of dimension $n\geq3$, with compact transversal $(M_0,g_0)$, and let $q_1,q_2\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ,\mathbb R)$. Assume zero is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue of either $-\Delta_g+q_j$, assume the unweighted scalar geodesic ray transform on $M_0$ is injective on compactly supported smooth functions, and suppose the full Schrödinger Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps agree:
$$\Lambda_{q_1}=\Lambda_{q_2}:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M).$$
Then $q_1=q_2$ on $M$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded smooth domain whose Euclidean metric is isometric to the product metric $dx_1^2\oplus g_0$ on a compact subdomain of $\mathbb R\times D^\circ$, where $(D,g_0)$ is a compact connected simple Riemannian surface with smooth boundary. Let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive. If their full physical scalar conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps agree on every boundary datum, then $\gamma_1=\gamma_2$ in $\overline\Omega$.

title: Scalar Calderón maps and conditional uniqueness — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A product geometry with an injective simple-surface transversal

references.title: Dos Santos Ferreira, Kurylev, Lassas, and Salo, The Calderon problem in transversally anisotropic geometries (2016)
references.locator: Section 1, product CTA geometry and simple transversal examples.

items.statement:
Let $D=\{x'\in\mathbb R^2:|x'|\leq1\}$ with its Euclidean metric and let
$$M=\{(x_1,x')\in\mathbb R\times D:x_1^2+4|x'|^2\leq1\}$$
with the restricted Euclidean product metric. Then $M$ is a compact smooth three-dimensional product subdomain compactly contained in $\mathbb R\times D^\circ$, and the transversal $D$ is a simple surface whose unweighted scalar geodesic ray transform is injective on real-valued compactly supported smooth functions.

items.title: Matching boundary jets without interior equality

references.title: Mikko Salo, Applications of microlocal analysis to inverse problems (2019)
references.locator: Section 5, Theorem 5.1, boundary determination of the full conductivity Taylor series.

items.statement:
On the unit ball $\Omega=B(0,1)\subset\mathbb R^n$, define
$$\psi(x)= \begin{cases} \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{1}{1-4|x|^2}\right),&|x|<1/2,\\ 0,&|x|\geq1/2. \end{cases}$$
For any $\epsilon\ne0$ with $|\epsilon|\|\psi\|_\infty<1$, the positive conductivities $\gamma_1\equiv1$ and $\gamma_2=1+\epsilon\psi$ agree with all orders of derivatives at $\partial\Omega$ but are unequal in the interior. This example shows that equality of all boundary conductivity jets alone does not imply interior equality; it makes no assertion that the two full DN maps agree.

items.title: A partial-data configuration outside the full-data theorem

references.title: Dos Santos Ferreira, Kurylev, Lassas, and Salo, The Calderon problem in transversally anisotropic geometries (2016)
references.locator: Theorem 1.2, scope of the full-data Schrödinger uniqueness result.

items.statement: Let $\Omega=B(0,1)\subset\mathbb R^3$ and let $\Gamma=\{x\in\partial\Omega:x_3>1/2\}$, a proper nonempty open boundary cap. A measurement protocol that knows only $\Lambda_\gamma f|_\Gamma$ for inputs $f\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)$ is a partial-data protocol. It is outside the full-data conductivity uniqueness theorem, whose hypothesis is equality of the DN operators on every boundary input; this example asserts no nonuniqueness for the partial-data protocol.
